rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daytime is when light spreads; legally it runs from dawn to sunset, though its basic sense runs from sunrise to sunset.
rows.anchor: النهار الوقت الذي ينتشر فيه الضوء وهو في الشرع ما بين طلوع الفجر إلى غروب الشمس وفي الأصل ما بين طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nushūr can mean spreading: daylight is when people spread out to seek their livelihood, as in 28:73.
rows.anchor: أي وجعل النهار ذا نشور أي انتشار ينتشر فيه الناس لطلب المعاش وابتغاء الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nushūr means resurrection: daylight is rising from sleep, which models the raising of the dead.
rows.anchor: أو من نشر الميت إذا عاد حيا أي وجعل النهار زمام بعث من ذلك السبات والنوم كبعث الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the resurrection reading, the phrase omits a genitive and substitutes its complement, intensifying the identification with resurrection itself.
rows.anchor: على حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه أي نفس البعث على الطريق المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep and waking are inward models of death and resurrection.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن النوم واليقظة انموذج للموت والنشور

rows.speaker: لقمان عليه السلام
rows.claim: Luqman tells his son that being awakened after sleep resembles dying and then being resurrected.
rows.anchor: وعن لقمان عليه السلام : يا بني كما تنام فتوقظ كذلك تموت فتنشر

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawi couplet likewise compares sleep with death.
rows.anchor: نوم ما ون شد اخ الموت أي فلان زين برادر آن برادرا بدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse permits sleep only to the extent needed to relieve bodily fatigue.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية رخصة للمنام بقدر دفع الضرورة وهو فتور البدن

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual elders say sleep rests the body, whereas spiritual disciplines tire it, so the two are opposed.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : النوم راحة للبدن والمجاهدات إتعاب البدن فيتضادان

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Sleep closes the outward senses so the senses of the heart can open.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة النوم سد حواس الظاهر لفتح حواس القلب

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: The holy spirit, divine subtlety, or rational soul is a stranger imprisoned in the low body and occupied with maintaining it while one is awake.
rows.anchor: الحكمة في النوم أن الروح القدسي أو اللطيفة الربانية أو النفس الناطقة غريبة جدا في هذا الجسم السفلي

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: In sleep the spirit returns to its original abode and rests among spirits, receiving unseen meanings represented through images in the visible world; this underlies dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: فإذا نام ذهب إلى مكانه الأصلي ومعدنه الذاتي فيستريح بواسطة لقاء الأوراح ومعرفة المعاني والغيوب

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: When a spiritual striver abandons sleep and rest, the four elements dissolve and the heart is unveiled to see the dominion of spirits and long for God.
rows.anchor: عليه أجزاء الأركان الأربعة من الترابية والمائية والنارية والهوائية فيعرى القلب حينئذ عن الحجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shah Shuja is said to have avoided sleep for thirty years, then seen God in a dream one night and thereafter carried a pillow and lay down wherever he went.
rows.anchor: كما حكي عن شاه شجاع أنه لم ينم ثلاثين سنة فاتفق أنه نام ليلة فرأى الحق سبحانه في منامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question is a resumption explaining the preceding exchange.
rows.anchor: {قال} استئناف بياني. {هل يسمعونكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means whether idols hear their invocations; a genitive is omitted because the addressee itself is not audible.
rows.anchor: أي : يسمعون دعاءكم على حذف المضاف فإن كم ليس من قبيل المسموعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural masculine form reflects the idolaters' treating their idols as rational beings.
rows.anchor: والواو بحسب زعمهم فإنهم كانوا يجرون الأصنام مجرى العقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the time when they call on the idols with their needs and expect a response.
rows.anchor: وقت دعائكم لحوائجكم فيستجيبون لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the idols benefit their worshippers in return for worship.
rows.anchor: {أو ينفعونكم} على عبادتكم لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also asks whether they can harm people if worship is withheld, since worship must bring benefit or avert harm.
rows.anchor: أو يضرونكم بترك العبادة إذ لا بد للعبادة من جلب نفع أو دفع ضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كذلك is governed by يفعلون and is the second object of وجدنا.
rows.anchor: منصوب بقوله : {يفعلون} وهو مفعول ثان لوجدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit the idols cannot hear, benefit, or harm, and confess they followed their fathers as their only support.
rows.anchor: وجدناهم يعبدون مثل عبادتنا فاقتدينا بهم اعترفوا بأنها بمعزل من السمع والمنفعة والمضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet warns truth-seekers not to follow an imitator's path to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: خواهي بسوى كعبه تحقيق ره برى ي بري مقلدكم كرده ره مرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is perfection in knowledge and action, qualifying one for divine vicegerency and leadership; knowledge without fitting action does not make its possessor wise.
rows.anchor: كمالا في العلم والعمل استعد به لخلافة الحق ورياسة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining the righteous can mean being enabled in knowledge, deeds, and character to join the perfected, or being reunited with them in Paradise.
rows.anchor: ووفقني من العلوم والأعمال والأخلاق لما ينظمني في زمرة الكاملين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's answer to Abraham's prayer is stated in 2:130: he is among the righteous in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: فقد أجابه تعالى حيث قال : {وإنه فى الاخرة لمن الصالحين}

words: وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍۢ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks for standing and a good reputation that endures until Judgment; all nations love and praise him.
rows.anchor: جاها وحسن صيت في الدنيا يبقى أثره إلى يوم الدين ولذلك ما من أمة إلا وهم محبون له مثنون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means good praise and a good name among later peoples; tongue stands for the means by which praise spreads and remembrance lasts.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الثناء الحسن والقبول العام باللسان لكون اللسان سببا في ظهوره وانتشاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lasting good name indicates God's pleasure and love; when God loves a servant, creation, even fish and birds, is made to love him.
rows.anchor: دولة عظيمة من حيث كونه دليلا على رضى الله عنه ومحبته والله تعالى إذا أحب عبدا يلقي محبته إلى أهل السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata reads the prayer as asking that Muhammad's community praise and bear witness for Abraham, since God made them accepted witnesses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أي أطلق لسان أمة محمد بالثناء والشهادة لي فإنك قد جعلتهم شداء مقبولين

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says Abraham asks God for praise throughout all nations and religious communities.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : اللهم ارزقني الثناء في جميع الأمم والملل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good remembrance truly comes through excellent deeds, good character, and a gentle tongue; these prompt later people to follow Abraham, earning him their reward as well.
rows.anchor: وإنما يحصل في الحقيقة بالفعل الجميل والخلق الحسن واللسان اللين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to mention of the Qur'an, not the Qur'an itself.
rows.anchor: أي : وإن ذكر القرآن لا عينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubur is the plural of zabūr, meaning books; the Qur'an's mention and the final Prophet's coming were in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: واحدها زبور بمعنى الكتاب مثل رسل ورسول ، أي لفي الكتب المتقدمة

words: أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ ءَايَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza denies a negative; the waw coordinates with an omitted clause, لهم is circumstantial, and the pronoun refers to Quraysh. آية precedes its subject for emphasis.
rows.anchor: الهمزة لإنكار النفي والواو للعطف على مقدر ولهم حال من آية والضمير راجع إلى مشركي قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelite scholars such as Abdullah ibn Salam knew the Qur'an's described traits from their books, making their knowledge a sign of the Qur'an's divine origin and the Messenger's truth.
rows.anchor: كعبد الله ن سلام ونحوه بنعوته المذكورة في كتبهم ويعلموا من أنزل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccans asked Jews of Medina about Muhammad and his mission; they replied that it was his time and the Torah described him.
rows.anchor: مكة بعثوا إلى يهود المدينة يسألونهم عن محمد وبعثته فقالوا : إن هذا لزمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's ahl are those especially close to him; here Moses addresses his wife and those with her in the valley of the Mount.
rows.anchor: أهل الإنسان من يختص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had stayed ten years in Midian with Shuayb, then set out with his family, Shuayb's daughter, for Egypt.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه مكث بمدين عند شعيب عشر سنين ثم سار بأهله بنت شعيب إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a very dark, cold night Moses lost the way; his wife went into labor, his flint failed, and a fire appeared by the Mount, so he told his family to wait.
rows.anchor: ليلة مظلمة شديدة البرد وقد أخذ امرأته الطلق فقدح فأصلد زنده

rows.speaker: التاج
rows.claim: The Taj glosses īnās as seeing; the root conveys something's appearance and what departs from estrangement.
rows.anchor: قال في "التاج" : (الإيناس : ديدن) والباب يدل على ظهور الشيء

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the fire was light, the light of the Lord of Might, seen Friday night at the mountain's right side in the Holy Land; the manifestation of light as fire was discussed in Sura Taha.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : النار هو النور وهو نور رب العزة رآه ليلة الجمعة عن يمين الجبل بالأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future prefix can indicate the distance of the road, or reinforce the promise that Moses will come even if delayed.
rows.anchor: والسين للدلالة على بعد المسافة أو لتحقيق الوعد بالإتيان وإن أبطأ فيكون للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises to bring news of the route from someone near the fire, or to return with a flame if no guide is there.
rows.anchor: أي بشعلة نار مقبوسة أي مأخوذة من معظم النار ومن أصلها إن لم أجد عندها من يدلني على الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shihāb is a bright flame and a qabaṣ is something taken from it; iqtabās is seeking it, later used for seeking knowledge and guidance.
rows.anchor: الشهاب الشعلة الساطعة من النار المتوقدة والقبس المتناول من الشعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom اقتبست منه نارا وعلما means taking fire from someone and, by extension, receiving knowledge from them.
rows.anchor: يقال : اقتبست منه نارا وعلما استفدته منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction with Moses' hopeful wording in 20:10: a person with strong hope may speak confidently while allowing events could turn otherwise.
rows.anchor: لا تدافع لأن الراجي إذا قوي رجاؤه يقول : سأفعل كذا مع تجويزه خلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hopes his family can warm themselves against the cold with the fire.
rows.anchor: رجاء أن تدفعوا البرد بحرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣilāʾ denotes a great fire, and iṣṭilāʾ is warming oneself by it.
rows.anchor: والصلاء النار العظيمة والاصطلاء (كرم شدن بآتش)

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say warming oneself by fire hardens the heart, and no report says the Prophet warmed himself at a fire.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الاصطلاء بالنار يقسي القلب ولم يرو أنه عليه السلام اصطلى بالنار

words: وجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس من دون الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Queen and her people worshipped the sun instead of God; Satan made this and their other acts of disbelief and sin attractive, diverting them from truth so they could not find guidance.
rows.anchor: حسن لهم أعمالهم القبيحة التي هي عبادة الشمس ونظائرها من أصناف الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is the object of purpose after an omitted lām: Satan turned them away so they would not prostrate.
rows.anchor: مفعول له للصد على حذف اللام منه أي فسدهم لئلا يسجدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase censures their failure to prostrate, which is why prostration is required at the end of these verses.
rows.anchor: وهو ذم لهم على ترك السجود فلذا وجب السجود عند تمام هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabʾ is something stored and concealed; God brings forth hidden things in heaven and earth, such as snow, rain, plants, and water.
rows.anchor: الخبأ يقال للمدخر المستور أي يظهر ما هو مخبوء ومخفي فيها كائنا ماكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden refers to what hearts conceal and the manifest to what tongues and limbs disclose; mentioning both broadens the scope and stresses equal divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: بالألسنة والجوارح وذكر ما تعلنون لتوسيع دائرة العلم للتنبيه على تساويهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet says not even a grain is hidden from God's knowledge; the concealed and manifest are alike to Him.
rows.anchor: برو علم يك ذره وشيده نيست كه نهان ويدا بنزدش يكيست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means strength, here the period from eighteen to thirty; the singular form is built on a plural pattern.
rows.anchor: أي : قوته وهو ما بين ثماني عشرة سنة إلى ثلاثين واحد على بناء الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiwāʾ means becoming balanced and mature in intellect; Moses reached this maturity at forty, as 46:15 indicates.
rows.anchor: والاستواء اعتدال الشيء في ذاته أي اعتدل عقله وكمل بأن بلغ أربيعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's account says only that he reached full strength because he received revelation in youth while in the well; Moses received revelation after forty.
rows.anchor: وفي يوسف {بلغ أشده} (يوسف : 22) فحسب لأنه أوحى إليه في صباه حين كونه في البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift of judgment means prophethood, while knowledge means knowledge of religion.
rows.anchor: أي : نبوة {وعلما} بالدين.

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says the account mentions the announcement of prophethood and that God made Moses a prophet after the migration, on his return from Midian to Egypt.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ذكر انباي نبوت دراثناي اين قضيه) أي معه أنه تعالى استنبأه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority holds that Muhammad was commissioned at forty; some extend the same age to every prophet.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن نبينا عليه السلام بعث على رأس الأربعين وكذا كل نبي عند البعض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others reject forty as a required age for prophets, citing Jesus at thirty-three, Joseph at eighteen, and John at two or three; Sahl al-Tustari attained spiritual knowledge before puberty.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : اشتراط الأربعين في حق الأنبياء ليس بشيء لأن عيسى عليه السلام نبىء ورفع إلى السماء وهو ابن ثلاث وثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine gifts reach a servant when their time comes, however long the delay; seekers should await God's favor without despair, since He rewards those who do good.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه على أن العطية الإلهية تصل إلى العبد وإن طال العهد إذا جاء أوانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and his mother were doers of good and pious in their early years; God rewards anyone who joins their company with the best recompense.
rows.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على أنهما كانا محسنين في عملهما متقيين في عنفوان عمرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman gave a beggar a bite, then a wolf snatched her child; after her prayer, a rescuer pulled the child unharmed from the wolf's mouth, repaying her charity.
rows.anchor: حكي : أن امرأة كانت تتعشى فسألها سائل فقامت ووضعت في فمه لقمة ثم وضعت ولدها في موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lover approaching God by way of trial fears that misguided people will obstruct arrival; fear accompanies the seeker until the goal is reached, so he prays for arrival.
rows.anchor: فإذا أقبل العاشق من طريق الامتحان إلى الحق خاف وترقب أن يلحقه أحد من أهل الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawajjaha means turning one's face in a direction; tilqāʾ is a verbal noun used as an adverb meaning toward or opposite.
rows.anchor: التوجه (روى باخيري كردن) والتلقاء تفعال من لقيت وهو مصدر اتسع فيه فاستعمل ظرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian was Shuayb's village by the Red Sea, named for Midian son of Abraham and Keturah, who settled there; it lay outside Pharaoh's domain and eight days from Egypt.
rows.anchor: ومدين قرية شعيب عليه السلام على بحر القلزم سميت باسم مدين بن إبراهيم عليه السلام من امرأته قنطورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means Moses turned his face toward Midian and headed toward its vicinity.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لما جعل موسى وجهه نحو مدين وصار متوجها إلى جانبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses speaks in trust and good expectation of God, though he does not know the roads.
rows.anchor: (باخود كفتت) توكلا على الله وحسن ظن به وكان لا يعرف الطرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-sabīl means the middle, straight road; a sabīl is a route customarily traveled.
rows.anchor: وسطه ومستقيمه والسبيل من الطرق ما هو معتاد السلوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three routes appeared; Moses took the middle one. His pursuers searched the other routes, thinking a fox would avoid the middle, and failed to find him.
rows.anchor: فظهر له ثلاث طرق فأخذ الوسطى وجاء الطلاب عقبيه فقالوا : إن الفار لا يأخذ الطريق الوسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Moses' face was toward Midian, his heart was turned toward God, making the journey a path of longing for encounter.
rows.anchor: فرموده كه روى مبارك بناحيه مدين داشت أمادلش متوجه بحضرت ذو المدين بود

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret Midian as the realm of pre-eternity and post-eternity; Moses sensed reality's breath there and turned toward it for vision and encounter.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : مدين إشارة إلى عالم الأزل والأبد فوجد موسى نسيم الحقيقة من جانبها

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The saying about finding the Breath of the Merciful from Yemen is read as sensing truth's breeze from Uways al-Qarani's heart; saintly lands and meetings bring blessings.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "إني لأجد نفس الرحمن من قبل اليمن" مخبرا عن وجدان نسيم الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wurūd means coming to water; its opposite, ṣudūr, is returning from it.
rows.anchor: الورود إتيان الماء وضده الصدور وهو

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat says wurūd originally means heading for water, then came to be used more broadly.
rows.anchor: وفي "المفردات" : الورود أصله قصد الماء ثم يستعمل في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses reached the well of Midian, three miles or less from the town, where people watered their livestock.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ولما وصل موسى وجاء {ماء مدين} وهو بئر على طرف المدينة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses arrived so emaciated from hunger that green vegetable matter could be seen through his belly.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ورده وإنه ليتراءى خضرة البقل في بطنه من الهزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses found a large group watering their animals by the well.
rows.anchor: أي جانب البئر وفوق شفيرها {أمة من الناس} جماعة كثيرة منهم

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: The two women were Shafuriyya and Layya, daughters of Yathrun, whom al-Suhayli identifies as Shuayb.
rows.anchor: صفورياء وليا ابنتا يثرون ويثرون هو شعيب قاله السهيلي في كتاب "التعريف"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhūdān means restraining, turning back, or pushing their sheep away from the well.
rows.anchor: الذود والكف والطرد والدفع أي تمنعان أغنامهما عن التقدم إلى البئر

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says Moses went over to them because prophets have innate compassion, and did so gently.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (از آنجاكه شفقت ذاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khatb is an important matter that prompts much discussion; Moses asks why they are holding back and not watering like the others.
rows.anchor: الخطب الأمر العظيم الذي يكثر فيه التخاطب أي ما شأنكما فيما أنتما عليه من التأخر والذود

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some ask how Moses could speak to two unrelated women; the answer is that he was safe from temptation and protected from it.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : كيف استجاز موسى أن يكلم امرأتين أجنبيتين والجواب كان آمنا على نفسه معصوما من الفتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy is that the Prophet could marry without witnesses because he was protected from denying or being accused of denying the marriage.
rows.anchor: كان للرسول التزوج بامرأة من غير الشهود لأن الشهود لصيانة العقد عن التجاحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿin, like qiyām and qāʾim; marʿā is pasture, and a caretaker of people or animals is a rāʿin.
rows.anchor: والرعاء بالكسر جمع راع كقيام جمع قائم ما يرعاء والمرعى موضع الرعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says everyone is responsible for those in their care; some distinguish animal herders from human shepherds, meaning rulers.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "كلكم مسؤول عن رعيته" قيل : الرعاء هم الذين يرعون المواشي والرعاة هم الذين يرعون الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women waited until the shepherds took their animals away after watering, avoiding competition and mixing with men, then watered with what remained.
rows.anchor: حذرا من مخالطة الرجال فإذا انصرفوا سقينا من فضل مواشيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Objects of watering, restraining, and sending away are omitted because the actions themselves matter and motivated Moses to help them.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول السقي والذود والإصدار لما أن الغرض هو بيان تلك الأفعال أنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father, Shuayb, was old or great in rank and honor; unable to go out, he had to send them to tend and water the animals.
rows.anchor: كبير السن أو القدر والشرف لا يستطيع أن يخرج فيرسلنا للرعي والسقي اضطرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A contemporary who sees a lesson in the unnoticed livestock of a prophet grasps it: herdsmen may not recognize prophets, as villagers may not know prophetic law, and believers are few.
rows.anchor: ومن قال من المعاصرين فيه عبرة أن مواشي النبي لم يلتفت إليها فقد أتى بالعبرة لأن الراعي لا يعرف ما النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses completes ten years, that extra service is a voluntary favor from him, not an obligation imposed by Shuayb.
rows.anchor: عشر سنين في الخدمة والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb does not want to burden Moses with the full ten years or exhausting work; hardship comes from what divides one's judgment and effort.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق المشقة من الشق فإن ما يصعب عليك بشق اعتقادك في إطاقته ويوزع رأيك في مزاولته

rows.speaker: بعض العرفاء
rows.claim: Some knowers say Shuayb foresaw Moses would reach completion and need no more spiritual training after eight years, with perfection of perfection at ten and independence beyond striving.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العرفاء : رأى شعيب بنور النبوة أنه يبلغ إلى درجة الكمال في ثماني حجج ولا يحتاج إلى التربية بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation implies Moses was thirty when he made the agreement, returned after ten years, and was commissioned on the road; the author relates this to completion of the path of annihilation and subsistence.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : اقتضى هذا التأويل أن عمر موسى وقتئذ كان ثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb's righteousness here means good treatment, gentleness, and keeping his covenant.
rows.anchor: في حسن المعاملة ولين الجانب والوفاء بالعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification God willing is for blessing and entrusting the matter to God's enabling grace, not making Shuayb's righteousness conditional.
rows.anchor: ومراده بالاستثناء التبرك به وتفويض الأمر إلى توفيقه لا تعليق صلاحه بمشيئته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Shuayb wept from love of God until blind; asked whether from longing for Paradise or fear of Hell, he answered that he loved God and did not care what God did, and God promised him the joy of meeting and gave him Moses to serve.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "بكى شعيب النبي عليه السلام من حب الله حتى عمي فرد الله عليه بصره وأوحى الله إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' flight from Pharaoh to Shuayb signifies a seeker's move from the commanding soul to the heart, away from an evil companion toward a good guide, whom he serves sincerely and steadily.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن في فرار موسى من فرعون إلى شعيب إشارة إلى أنه ينبغي لطالب الحق أن يسافر من مقام النفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham is reported to have carried wood for seventeen years.
rows.anchor: روي : أن إبراهيم بن أدهم كان يحمل الحطب سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The service agreement alludes to the Sufi path: having disciples serve their spiritual guides follows the practice of prophets.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : {على أن تأجرنى ثمانى حجج} إشارة إلى طريق الصوفية وأن استخدامهم للمريدين من سنن الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hafiz couplet pictures one attaining the goal only after years serving Shuayb devotedly.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : شبان وادي أيمن كهي رسد بمراد كه ند سال بجان خدمت شعيب كند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first mā is a subject carrying a conditional sense, which accounts for the fāʾ in its predicate; the following mā is different.
rows.anchor: {وما} مبتدأ متضمنة لمعنى الشرط لدخول الفاء في خبرها بخلاف الثانية

rows.speaker: الوسيط
rows.claim: The address is to Meccan disbelievers, and the gifts are worldly means.
rows.anchor: أعطيتم والخطاب لكفار مكة كما في "الوسيط"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly gifts are brief means for enjoyment and adornment that soon perish, like household goods; they are called mataʿ because they do not last.
rows.anchor: أي : فهو شيء شأنه أن يتمتع ويتزين به أياما قلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is with God is reward, better in itself because its pleasure is free of pain and worry, and more lasting because it is eternal.
rows.anchor: {وما} موصولة أي الذي حصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question urges reflection: why trade the inferior, fleeting life and misery from disbelief and sin for the better reward and happiness of faith and obedience?
rows.anchor: ألا تتفكرون فلا تعقلون هذا الأمر الواضح فتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those meant by from among these are Arabs.
rows.anchor: {ومن هؤلاء} أي من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in whoever believes in it refers to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن {وما يجحد} الجحد نفي ما في القلب إثباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaḥd is denying what one's heart affirms or asserting what one's heart denies.
rows.anchor: الجحد نفي ما في القلب إثباته أو إثبات ما في القلب نفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the exalted Book verses highlights the clarity of their meanings and their evidence that the Book is from God.
rows.anchor: عبر عنه بالآيات للتنبيه على ظهور دلالته على معانيه وعلى كونه من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception refers to entrenched, obstinate disbelievers, whose disbelief blocks reflection leading to true knowledge.
rows.anchor: المتوغلون في الكفر المصممون عليه فإن ذلك يصدهم عن التأمل فيما يؤديهم إلى معرفة حقيقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the heart and divinely gifted inner knowledge should discuss with outward scholars gently and calmly, avoiding agitation of the commanding soul and increased denial.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن أرباب القلوب وأصحاب العلوم الباطنة الذين علومهم من مواهب الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom God guides accept unveiling's evidences and reach truth; those deprived of guidance deny them and move further from God.
rows.anchor: فمن رحمه الله منهم صدق الدلائل الكشفية والبراهين الحقية في دلالتها إلى الحق واهتدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi verses counsel receptivity and humility, warning against denying advice and praising the sound heart over proud cleverness.
rows.anchor: هركرا مشك نصيحت سودنيست لا جرم بابوى بدخوكرنيسبمغزرا خالى كن از انكار يار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disputation aimed at obstinacy or promoting falsehood cancels reward, but arguing truthfully to make truth clear is commanded.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المجادلة في الدين تبطل ثواب الأعمال إذا كانت تعنتا وترويحا للباطل وأما الجدال بالحق لإظهاره فمأمور به

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: When someone claimed to own his movements, stillness, divorce, and emancipation, Ali asked whether he owned them apart from God or with Him: either answer implied another owner or a partner.
rows.anchor: وقد جادل علي رضي الله عنه شخصا قال : إني أملك حركاتي وسكناتي وطلاق زوجتي وأعتق أمتي

words: وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُوا۟ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِن كِتَٰبٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Qur'an was revealed, Muhammad did not customarily recite any revealed book or write one.
rows.anchor: {ولا تخطه} ولا أن تكتب كتابا من الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭṭ means drawing something long and is used for writing; the right hand is mentioned because people usually write with it.
rows.anchor: والخط كالمد ويقال لما له طول ويعبر عن الكتابة بالخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of the right hand reflects the custom of right-handed writing, not an implication that left-handed writing is impossible; it is exceptionally rare.
rows.anchor: يعني ذكر اليمين لكون الكتابة غالبا باليمين لا أنه لا يخط بيمينه ويخط بشماله

rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: The Shia say Muhammad could write before revelation but was forbidden by revelation; they read the phrase as a prohibition and say it does not deny earlier writing.
rows.anchor: قال الشيعة : إنه عليه السلام كان يحسن الخط قبل الوحي ثم نهي عنه بالوحى

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar notes a rare reading with fatḥa on ṭāʾ as a prohibition, but says the correct view is that the Prophet did not write.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : قرىء ولا تخطه بالفتح على النهي وهو شاذ والصحيح أنه لم يكن يكتب

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima rejects the Shia argument: if the phrase were prohibitive, ṭāʾ should be subjunctive, or the verb would be intensified as لا تخططه.
rows.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : قول الشيعة مردود لأن لا تخطه لو كان نهيا لكان ينصب الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Muhammad been accustomed to reciting and writing, falsifiers could suspect he learned or copied the Qur'an from earlier books; since he was not, there is no basis for doubt.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : لعله تعلمه أو التقته من كتب الأوائل وحيث لم تكن كذلك لم يبق في شأنك منشأ ريب أصلا

rows.speaker: المختار
rows.claim: Al-Mukhtar defines rayb as doubt.
rows.anchor: قال في "المختار" : الريب الشك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes rayb as a suspicion exposed as false, irāba as one not dispelled, and irtiyāb as similar to irāba; he cites the believers' lack of doubt in 74:31.
rows.anchor: قال في "المختار" : الريب الشك. قال الراغب : الريب أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mubṭil brings falsehood, the opposite of a muḥiqq, who brings truth.
rows.anchor: والمبطل من يأتي بالباطل وهو نقيض المحق وهو من يأتي بالحق

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat says ibṭāl means destroying or removing something, and can describe someone whose assertion has no reality; 8:8 speaks of establishing truth and nullifying falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : الإبطال يقال في إفساد الشيء وإزالته حقا كان الشيء أو باطلا
